stories.headline: Israel-Iran de-escalation remains a lead global concern
stories.summary: Live world-news coverage this morning led with Benjamin Netanyahu crediting Donald Trump for helping de-escalate Israel-Iran tensions, keeping Middle East stability at the center of the global news cycle.
stories.pastoral_note: Pray for peacemakers and for believers in the region to embody the reconciling presence of Christ when nations are tempted toward retaliation.

stories.headline: Church attack in India injures at least 25 worshippers
stories.summary: International Christian Concern reports that a Hindu nationalist mob attacked a worship service in Chhattisgarh, India, injuring at least 25 Christians, including the pastor's pregnant wife, amid rising concern over anti-conversion pressures.
stories.pastoral_note: Name persecuted believers in prayer, not as distant victims but as family; their courage helps the wider church remember that worship is costly and precious.

stories.headline: Canadian leaders see Gen Z stirring fresh religious curiosity
stories.summary: CTV's feature on a return to faith notes church leaders reporting renewed attendance after decades of decline, with Gen Z often named as a key driver of the shift.
stories.pastoral_note: The moment calls for less panic about secularization and more readiness to receive spiritually hungry young adults with depth, hospitality, and a clear gospel.

stories.headline: Tech firms turn to faith leaders for AI ethics guidance
stories.summary: AP reports that representatives from companies including Anthropic and OpenAI met with religious leaders at a Faith-AI Covenant roundtable to discuss moral norms for artificial intelligence.
stories.pastoral_note: This is a rare public admission that technical power needs moral wisdom; churches should speak about human dignity, formation, and discernment with confidence and humility.

stories.headline: Purpose can backfire when systems block meaningful impact
stories.summary: Harvard Business Review warns that purpose-driven organizations create an implicit promise: employees expect to make a meaningful difference, but rules, metrics, and processes can make them withdraw when that promise is frustrated.
stories.pastoral_note: Churches should not merely talk about mission; leaders need to remove friction so volunteers and staff can actually touch the life-giving work they were called into.

stories.headline: Fraser Valley market favours buyers as inventory tops 10,000 listings
stories.summary: The Fraser Valley Real Estate Board's May 2026 report says inventory surpassed 10,000 listings, sales rose modestly from April, and benchmark prices eased slightly after two months of gains.
stories.pastoral_note: Housing pressure remains a discipleship issue: people are making major decisions under uncertainty, and the church can offer both practical care and a steadier imagination of home.

stories.headline: A 39-year Bible translation bears fruit for 3,800 Notsi speakers
stories.summary: Christianity Today reports that the Notsi people of Papua New Guinea celebrated a New Testament in their mother tongue after a translation effort spanning nearly four decades.
stories.pastoral_note: This is a beautiful reminder that God is not a foreign God; the Word comes near, speaks the language of a people, and dignifies small places with kingdom attention.

stories.headline: Russell Moore says apologetics needs confidence more than combat
stories.summary: In Christianity Today, Russell Moore argues that many people come to faith not through public debate victories but through ordinary grace, faithful churches, Scripture, and embodied witness.
stories.pastoral_note: For evangelism, the edge may be less about winning arguments and more about carrying the Word with quiet confidence, relational credibility, and the surprise of grace.
